mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate environment, as measured by FEDFUNDS, indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5.0% over three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending power and corporate earnings growth, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0% for three consecutive months, or the Rank IC over a 2-year window is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in demand, which triggers a negative feedback loop in corporate revenue expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline from prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline from prior month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of manufacturing supply chain disruption, as indicated by a sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0, corporate output constraints reduce profit margins and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO is below 100.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 240.0 for two consecutive months signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 240.0 for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over a 2-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Residential construction activity (HOUST) serves as a leading indicator of household spending strength, and higher HOUST values consistently predict positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to improved corporate earnings outlook.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and an increase in CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 240.0 signals a monetary policy response to inflation, which initially boosts economic activity but eventually leads to higher real rates and negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 240.0 and FEDFUNDS declines from prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 240.0 and FEDFUNDS declines from prior month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In tight labor markets (UNRATE below 4.5%) with strong employment growth (PAYEMS above 145,000), consumer spending and corporate earnings are supported, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE < 4.5% and PAYEMS > 145000, or the Rank IC over a 3-year window is below 0.03.
